tasks.short: Monitor environmental impacts and land degradation

steps.what: Define the environmental monitoring boundary, comparison period and relevant impact indicators
Observe actual site conditions and collect the required environmental measurements
Enter the actual monitoring observations with location, time, units and method references
Tabulate comparable monitoring periods and plot the agreed environmental impact indicators
Check and interpret environmental changes, method differences and possible alternative causes
Write the actual internal monitoring finding and its limitations

tasks.design: Configure a native {DATA_PLATFORM} query and {SPREADSHEET} chart for the existing environmental indicators after the ecologist collects and enters the actual observations. Retain comparison checks, manual mapping repair and the existing internal monitoring finding; no field measurement or causal judgement is automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring indicator tables and plots may be rebuilt for each monitoring period.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed queries and charts can repeat agreed calculations on source-linked entries.
tasks.still_hard: Changing methods, seasonal effects and site conditions can make apparent trends misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist determines whether observed change supports an environmental impact conclusion.
tasks.altitude: Remove repeated tabulation inside actual environmental monitoring.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed data queries and charts can reproduce environmental monitoring indicators from checked entries.

assumptions: Shares are hypotheses for a field-monitoring and manual-chart branch, not measured baselines.
The ecologist produces location, timestamp, indicator, value, unit, method and quality flag in s2 and s3; missing metadata is resolved manually.
Native configuration is tested before code; existing automated charts yield no additional labour saving.
Failed mappings and noncomparable periods are manually repaired or excluded in retained s5 and reduce benefit.
The monitoring finding already informs impact follow-up; it is not a new trailing record or a regulator filing.
research_questions: Can the repeated plots be reproduced without hiding method or quality changes?

already_counted.description: Capture actual data in s2 and s3 and check and repair comparisons in s5.

incremental.description: Amortised indicator query, unit and chart checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Repeated plotting removes 15 hours less 1 upkeep, net 14. Cautious case: changed sampling locations and methods force manual comparison reconstruction, leaving only 3 hours of stable-indicator plots removed and 2 net; reconstruction consumes the rest of the nominal benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find and verify the actual energy, pollutant, environment and industrial-process information sources
Map and check actual database fields, identifiers, units, dates and source permissions
outputs: checked import mapping and source rows

steps.what: Enter the mapped ecological information into the actual maintained database
inputs: checked import mapping and source rows

steps.what: Reconcile imported records, resolve duplicates and maintain provenance and database quality

tasks.design: Test native {DATA_PLATFORM} mapped imports to replace actual re-keying of verified source rows into the ecological database. The ecologist prepares mappings and nonstructured source content manually, reconciles updates and repairs rejected rows; ordinary internal database saves do not gain an approval stage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified source data can still be typed again into the maintained database.
tasks.enabler_now: Native mapped imports can transfer compatible source rows and preserve provenance fields.
tasks.still_hard: Source credibility, unit interpretation and duplicate identity require curation.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist decides what the database can reliably claim about ecological change.
tasks.altitude: Replace real re-keying while retaining database curation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: governed databases can import mapped structured rows with provenance and validation checks.

assumptions: Shares describe an unmeasured manual re-entry branch; current automatic import runtime yields no saving.
Source publishers produce existing source datasets; the ecologist verifies them in s1 and produces schema mapping, identifiers, units, dates and provenance in s2.
Nonstructured documents require manual extraction in s2; no labelled dataset arrives free.
Incompatible or rejected rows stop for manual entry and repair in retained s2 and s4, reducing benefit.
The database already serves actual ecological analysis; no new public data publication is included.
research_questions: Which source rows are genuinely re-keyed today after mapping and curation?

already_counted.description: Prepare mappings and manual extraction in s2 and reconcile or repair database updates in s4.

incremental.description: Amortised schema, import and provenance regression checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Mapped import removes 30 re-entry hours less 1.5 upkeep, net 28.5. Cautious case: source schemas and units are mostly incompatible and require manual extraction and re-entry, leaving only 6 hours of compatible row transfer removed and 4.5 net; fallback work consumes the rest of the nominal benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze interactions between human behavior and environmental change

steps.what: Review the actual behavioral and environmental evidence, definitions, sampling and source limitations
Choose the analytical design and prepare actual variables, coding and causal assumptions
Calculate the specified behavioral and environmental associations and comparison tables
Interpret how human behavior affects and is affected by environmental change
Write the actual analysis findings, methodological limits and supported conclusions

tasks.design: Configure existing {DATA_PLATFORM} statistical routines and {SPREADSHEET} comparison tables for the ecologist's explicit analysis specification. Retain evidence coding, causal choices, output checks and the actual written findings; automated associations are not treated as causal conclusions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring specified calculations and comparison tables may be assembled manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native statistical routines can reproduce explicit calculations from checked variables.
tasks.still_hard: Confounding, feedback and incompatible behavioral measures can invalidate an interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist judges what the evidence supports about people and their environment.
tasks.altitude: Reduce calculation mechanics within a human research analysis.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native statistical routines can calculate explicitly specified associations and tables from prepared variables.

assumptions: Shares are unmeasured hypotheses for repeated manual calculation, not existing software runtime.
Evidence producers supply actual observations; the ecologist counts variable coding, missingness handling and specification in s1 and s2.
Missing or incompatible variables stop for manual recoding and calculation checks in s2 and s4; extra repair reduces benefit.
The existing written analysis is the actual output; no additional registry or public release is introduced.
research_questions: Which calculations repeat without changing the study's causal and variable definitions?

already_counted.description: Prepare and repair variable coding in s2 and check calculations and meaning in s4.

incremental.description: Amortised calculation, missingness and specification regression checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Repeated calculations remove 20 hours less 2 upkeep, net 18. Cautious case: noncomparable surveys and changed behavioral definitions require manual recoding and bespoke analysis, leaving only 3 hours of routine tabulation removed and 1 net; additional work consumes the rest of the nominal calculation benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend methods to reduce industrial environmental damage

steps.what: Verify the actual industrial process, environmental impacts and practical operating constraints
Evaluate methods to protect the environment or minimize damage from industrial production practices
Write the actual environmental protection recommendation with evidence and implementation conditions

loop.purpose: Draft recommendation prose from the ecologist's selected methods and evidence
loop.input: Verified process evidence, selected methods, trade-offs and implementation limits
loop.output: Source-linked recommendation draft without new technical claims
loop.check: Ecologist checks causal claims, technical conditions, omitted trade-offs and every numerical or source assertion against the evidence
loop.stop: Unsupported method or two failed revisions returns the prose to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native recommendation headings first; variable explanatory prose needs a bounded drafting loop

steps.what: Check and approve the final recommendation and its exact operational recipients
Send the approved recommendation to its approved operational recipients

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} recommendation headings before a bounded loop drafts prose from methods the ecologist has already evaluated. Check the completed recommendation and recipients before its separate {EMAIL} send; the design recommends changes without implementing process controls or committing spend.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected technical methods still need a clear evidence-grounded written recommendation.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can express selected methods without selecting them or inventing performance claims.
tasks.still_hard: Environmental trade-offs and practical feasibility remain process-specific.
tasks.human_edge: The ecologist takes responsibility for which methods deserve recommendation.
tasks.altitude: Assist recommendation prose while keeping technical selection and issue decisions human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded source-constrained drafting can express technical recommendations selected by an expert.

assumptions: Shares are unmeasured hypotheses for an existing written recommendation path.
The ecologist produces checked evidence in s1 and actual selected methods and conditions in s2; no technical option ranking is supplied free.
The final recommendation is actually read by operational decision makers; no new unused record is introduced.
Ordinary author saves are retained within drafting and have no gate; the approval concerns the actual recipient-bound issue.
research_questions: Does drafting remove prose time after checking all process-specific qualifications?

already_counted.description: Check generated claims in s3 and repair and verify the completed recommendation in s4.

incremental.description: Amortised source-link and technical-qualification regression checks.

approvals.approved_version: s4 exact final recommendation, supporting evidence version and named recipients; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Initial prose removes 25*0.20=5 hours less 0.8 upkeep, net 4.2. Cautious case: a bespoke production process needs almost all technical prose rewritten, leaving only 1 hour of routine introductory explanation removed and 0.2 net; rewrite work consumes the rest of the nominal drafting benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use source-linked data handling and bounded drafting while retaining ecological and social interpretation.
skills_to_grow: Separate technical method selection from explanatory prose
role.ambitious_version: An industrial ecologist works from reliable source-linked evidence and personally owns the environmental interpretation and recommended action.
